packs.scope: Decision frameworks for the current stable Project Zomboid branch. Back up saves and recheck build-specific behavior before changing an established world.

guides.title: Can you change zombie settings mid-save in Project Zomboid?
guides.description: A cautious test plan for changing zombie behavior in an existing Project Zomboid world without treating an unverified edit as reversible.
guides.question: Can I change zombie settings without abandoning my current save?
guides.answer: Treat a mid-save sandbox change as a migration, not a casual toggle. Duplicate the save first, record the current build and settings, change one variable in the copy, and verify both existing and newly loaded areas before trusting the result.
decisionRows: Confirm the save and game build are backed up
Change one zombie variable at a time
Compare behavior before adding more edits
Test an explored area and a newly loaded area
Keep or roll back based on both results
checklist: Record the current build number and sandbox values
Create a separate copy of the complete save directory
Make one controlled settings change in the copied world
Load an existing area and a newly visited area
Keep the original untouched until several sessions are stable
stopConditions: Stop if the copied world fails to load or loses expected data
Roll back if the change affects more systems than the one being tested
mistakes: Editing the only copy of a long-running world
Changing several population variables in one test
Assuming existing cells and new cells must update identically

guides.title: Project Zomboid trait planning by actual playstyle
guides.description: Choose character traits around the first jobs, risks, and recovery plan you will really use instead of copying a universal build.
guides.question: Which Project Zomboid traits fit the way I actually play?
guides.answer: Start from the jobs you expect to perform during the first week, then choose traits that reduce the risks you repeatedly face. A strong build is one whose disadvantages you can manage consistently, not the build with the most impressive spreadsheet total.

List the skills your base plan actually needs
Describe how it will be managed every day
Remove it if the answer is vague
checklist: Write down the first three jobs this character must perform
Identify the failure that ended the previous run
Match positive traits to repeated actions rather than rare events
Explain how every negative trait will be controlled
Keep one simpler backup build for comparison
stopConditions: Rework the build if one negative trait controls the entire run
Delay optimization when you cannot explain the first-week routine
mistakes: Copying a veteran build without the same habits
Buying skill efficiency that never supports the plan
Treating point balance as proof that the build is practical

guides.title: How to choose a first safehouse in Project Zomboid
guides.description: Compare access, visibility, escape routes, storage, and daily travel before investing supplies in an early Project Zomboid base.
guides.question: What makes an early safehouse worth committing to?
guides.answer: Choose the location that supports several safe daily loops and at least two exits. A larger building is not automatically safer: travel exposure, poor sight lines, difficult clearing, and one-way access can make an impressive base expensive to maintain.

Identify two exits and fallback buildings
Avoid a base with one trapped approach
Check storage, vehicles, farming, and noise
Commit only after a short trial stay
checklist: Clear and inspect the immediate perimeter
Walk two independent routes to essential supplies
Confirm more than one practical exit
Spend one night before moving irreplaceable equipment
Keep a small fallback cache away from the main building
stopConditions: Leave if daily travel repeatedly forces high-risk crossings
Do not commit if clearing the perimeter consumes more resources than the location saves
mistakes: Choosing only for building size
Ignoring vehicle access and blocked exits
Moving every valuable item before testing the area

guides.title: Project Zomboid mod conflict isolation checklist
guides.description: Find a broken Project Zomboid mod combination with a repeatable clean test instead of repeatedly damaging the main save.
guides.question: How do I identify which mod is breaking the game or save?
guides.answer: Reproduce the problem in a disposable profile, confirm the unmodded baseline, and restore mods in small groups. Keep the load order and game build fixed during each comparison so a successful launch actually tells you something.
decisionRows: Test a clean profile on the same build
Investigate the base game or local files first
Repeat with the same mods in controlled order

Record the game build and complete enabled-mod order

Restore mods in bounded groups rather than one random order

stopConditions: Stop using the main save when a test changes map or item data
Do not declare a fix until the same setup survives a restart
mistakes: Testing directly on the only valuable save
Changing build, mods, and load order together
Assuming one successful launch proves long-session stability

guides.title: Project Zomboid vehicle trip preparation checklist
guides.description: Plan fuel, storage, tools, alternate roads, and a return condition before turning a supply run into a stranded recovery mission.
guides.question: What should I check before taking a vehicle on a long supply run?
guides.answer: Prepare the return before planning the loot. Check the vehicle, fuel margin, route alternatives, repair needs, and what can be abandoned. The trip is ready when one blocked road or damaged part does not erase the entire run.

Abandon optional cargo before risking the only transport

guides.title: Project Zomboid build update save-safety checklist
guides.description: Revalidate saves, mods, settings, and rollback options before opening an established Project Zomboid world after a major build update.
guides.question: How should I reopen an old world after a major Project Zomboid update?
guides.answer: Preserve the old environment first. Record the previous build and mod list, duplicate the save, read the current official notes, and open only the copy. Test core inventory, map, vehicle, and base behavior before resuming normal play.

Decide whether to update now or remain on the old branch

packs.scope: Decision frameworks for the current Escape from Tarkov release. Exact weapon, ammunition, trader, task, and extraction details must be checked against the active patch and mode.

guides.title: Escape from Tarkov budget weapon choice by real access
guides.description: Choose a dependable Tarkov weapon around ammunition access, trader level, task needs, replacement cost, and recoil you can actually control.
guides.question: What should be my go-to gun at my current level and budget?
guides.answer: The best default is the platform you can replace with ammunition that suits the intended target and a configuration you can control. Compare complete recurring cost and access, not an isolated weapon statistic or a streamer build.

guides.title: Tarkov ammunition and armor assumption check
guides.description: Recheck current ammunition access, intended targets, armor assumptions, cost, and evidence before treating an old chart as a raid plan.

guides.answer: Trust the recommendation only after matching it to the current patch, mode, trader access, and expected targets. A chart can remain numerically accurate while becoming impractical because access, price, or common protection changed.

guides.title: Escape from Tarkov quest route planning checklist

guides.question: How should I plan a quest route without forcing one bad path?

guides.title: Escape from Tarkov extraction readiness checklist

guides.question: What should I verify before committing to an extraction route?

guides.title: Tarkov stash keep-or-sell triage
guides.description: Classify Tarkov stash items by near-term tasks, repeatable access, storage pressure, replacement cost, and current patch relevance.
guides.question: How do I decide what to keep instead of filling the stash?
guides.answer: Keep items tied to a near-term verified use, expensive replacement, or constrained access. Sell duplicates and speculative stock that blocks functional kits. The goal is not maximum theoretical value; it is a stash that supports the next several decisions.

guides.title: Escape from Tarkov wipe progression priorities
guides.description: Choose the next Tarkov progression goal by access, survival rate, task dependencies, equipment budget, and time available this wipe.
guides.question: What should I prioritize next during the current wipe?
guides.answer: Prioritize the bottleneck that unlocks several useful options, not the task with the loudest reward. Compare trader access, required maps, survival cost, and time. Work in short loops that still create value when one raid fails.

guides.title: Warframe returning-player priority plan

guides.question: What should I do first after returning to Warframe?
